title: Speech-to-text meal description in scan confirmation + automatic weekly summary feedback

requirements.summary: Add optional on-device speech-to-text dictation to the scan confirmation step with editable transcription and graceful fallback.
acceptanceCriteria: In the scan confirmation step (the page that currently shows “Confirm Food Details”), there is a clear control (e.g., a microphone button) to start/stop dictation.
Dictation converts the user’s spoken words into text in a visible editable text field.
The user can edit the transcribed text before saving.
If the browser/device does not support speech recognition or permission is denied, the UI shows an English message explaining the issue and still allows manual typing without blocking the flow.

file_operations.description: Create a React hook that wraps the browser Web Speech API (SpeechRecognition / webkitSpeechRecognition) to support start/stop dictation, interim/final transcript updates, and error states (not-supported, permission denied). Use only local/on-device speech recognition and expose English error messages for the UI.

Add an optional meal description field to the “Confirm Food Details” step and integrate dictation controls using the new useSpeechToText hook (microphone start/stop). Ensure transcription is shown in an editable text input/textarea, allow manual edits at any time, and show a clear English fallback message when speech recognition is unavailable or permission is denied without blocking saving.

requirements.summary: Persist the spoken/edited meal description from scan confirmation into saved entries and display it in existing entry list/details UI without breaking manual entry.
acceptanceCriteria: When saving an entry from the scan flow, the saved entry reflects the user’s edited dictated description (not only the auto-detected food name).
The stored description is visible wherever the app currently displays the entry label/details (e.g., today’s entries list and entry details dialog).
No existing manual-entry flow is broken by this change.

file_operations.description: Update the add-food-entry mutation to include a description string parameter and pass arguments in the correct order to the backend actor so the entry description is persisted. Keep description optional at call sites by allowing an empty string default.
Wire the scan confirmation’s editable description (including dictated/edited text) into the save action by passing it to useAddFoodEntry so it becomes the entry’s persisted description.

Ensure the manual add-entry flow continues to work by supplying a description value to useAddFoodEntry (default empty string). Optionally add a non-required 'Description' field if it fits the existing form layout, without changing required validation for the existing fields.
Display the entry description (when present) in the existing today entries list UI in a compact, readable way while keeping the existing foodLabel and calories display.
Add an English-labeled section in the entry details dialog to show the saved entry description (when non-empty) alongside existing nutrient details.

requirements.summary: Add an automatic “Weekly Summary (Last 7 Days)” section on the Dashboard showing totals/averages, a 1–10 score, and an English feedback message with an insufficient-data state.
acceptanceCriteria: The Dashboard includes a “Weekly Summary (Last 7 Days)” section that appears without the user needing to manually trigger generation.
The weekly summary displays: (1) last-7-days totals/averages (at minimum calories and macros), (2) a numeric score from 1 to 10, and (3) a short English feedback message.
When the score indicates the user is doing well, the summary shows an English congratulatory message.
If there is insufficient data (e.g., no entries in the last 7 days), the section shows an English empty/insufficient-data state rather than failing silently.

file_operations.description: Implement deterministic, fully local helper functions to compute last-7-days totals/averages (calories + macros), determine whether there is sufficient data, and produce a 1–10 score plus an English feedback message based on simple rules.

Create a Dashboard-ready Weekly Summary card component that renders: (1) calories/macros totals/averages, (2) a numeric 1–10 score, (3) an English feedback message (including congratulatory text when on track), and (4) an English insufficient-data state when last-7-days entries are missing.

Fetch the last 7 days of entries using existing useGetFoodEntries (rangeStart=today-6, rangeEnd=today) and render the new “Weekly Summary (Last 7 Days)” section automatically on the Dashboard using WeeklySummaryCard (no manual trigger). Ensure all user-facing labels are in English.

requirements.summary: Render the weekly 1–10 rating as a clear, visually engaging visualization consistent with existing Tailwind/shadcn styling.
acceptanceCriteria: The weekly summary shows a visual rating element that clearly communicates the 1–10 score at a glance.
The rating visualization and weekly summary card use existing Tailwind/Shadcn styling patterns used elsewhere in the app.
All user-facing labels in the weekly summary are in English.

file_operations.description: Create a reusable weekly rating visualization component that displays a 1–10 score at a glance (e.g., segmented scale or star-like markers) using existing Tailwind patterns and composed shadcn/ui primitives (do not modify anything under frontend/src/components/ui).
Integrate WeeklyRatingScale into the Weekly Summary card to visually represent the computed 1–10 score alongside the numeric value, keeping styling consistent with other Dashboard cards.

requirements.summary: Generate weekly feedback using deterministic local rules referencing the user’s stored body goal (if available) and last-7-days logged data, with concrete suggestions and per-user correctness.
acceptanceCriteria: Weekly feedback generation does not call any external services/APIs.
If the user has a body goal configured, the weekly feedback references it (e.g., “Lose Weight”, “Gain Muscle”) in English.
The app produces at least one concrete suggestion when the score is not high (e.g., suggest increasing protein if protein share is low), based only on logged data and simple rules.
The feature works per-user (no data leakage across principals).

file_operations.description: Extend the deterministic rules to incorporate the current user’s body goal (from the already-loaded user profile) into the English feedback text and ensure at least one actionable suggestion is produced when the score is not high, derived only from last-7-days totals/ratios.

Pass the current user’s body goal into the weekly feedback computation and render goal-referencing English text in the Weekly Summary UI. Ensure the component uses only the currently authenticated user’s entries/profile data already loaded on the Dashboard.

Wire the current user profile’s body goal (if available) into WeeklySummaryCard so the feedback references it and remains per-user (based on the caller-scoped entries returned by existing data hooks).
